I have farmed this wheat-maize land for 30 years, so I will start from what has worked for me before and only adjust a little. My land is only 3.8 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but I still do not want to hold back too much on fertilizer because if yield drops, that loss is bigger than wasting a little input. Here in Hebei, with well irrigation, I will keep the usual wheat-maize rotation on all 3.8 mu. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put fertilizer a bit heavier at the base, water about 3 times if the year is normal, and spray 2 times if disease and aphids show up. Wheat needs steady growth through winter and spring, so I will not let it go hungry early. After wheat harvest, I will quickly rotary till and plant summer maize. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because that has been the normal choice around here for years and the yield is better if management keeps up. I will feed maize mainly with nitrogen, keep some phosphorus and potassium under it, irrigate 2 times in a normal year, and spray about 2 times for weeds and insects. I do what I have seen work on fields around me: not too fancy, not too risky, but enough input to protect yield on irrigated land.
